speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry has reviewed the $140,000 lifetime CPF contribution threshold for eligibility under the Silver Support Scheme; and (b) what considerations guide any adjustments in light of cost-of-living changes affecting seniors reliant on CPF payouts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Ministry periodically reviews the eligibility criteria for the Silver Support Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government also provides various forms of support to help Singaporeans, including seniors, to cope with the cost-of-living concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This includes the Assurance Package, and the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Voucher schemes, which were enhanced in 2025.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If we take the Silver Support threshold of $140,000 as a share of the FRS a decade ago, the equivalent adjustment would bring this to around $191,000 today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Keeping in mind that the FRS itself represents the Government's own assessment of a basic standard of living in retirement, the rigidity of the equivalent CPF threshold for Silver Support is somewhat puzzling to me.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Would the Minister be willing to share the rationale for this seeming inconsistency between CPF FRS adjustments relative to the Silver Support threshold?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not think it is a like-for-like comparison.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: You need to look at the Silver Support Scheme in a holistic manner.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because we do have a number of other schemes that has come alongside the Silver Support Scheme to support our elderly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, there are also significant CPF enhancements that we are doing to support our elderly, the cost-of-living vouchers and the different packages – such as the Pioneer Generation Package to the Merdeka Generation Package to the Majulah Package.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They are all aimed at different sectors of uplifting our seniors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, in addition to the Silver Support Scheme, you need to look at it on a broader, a more comprehensive and a more holistic scale.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, we periodically review the parameters in which the Silver Support Scheme is improved and refined.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared earlier on in 2021, we expanded the coverage from $70,000 TCC over a lifetime, to $140,000.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This has resulted in a larger number of elderly Singaporeans becoming eligible.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In 2025, just a year ago, we enhanced the quarterly payouts by some 20%.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have also expanded the household per capita income by almost 28%.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, you need to look at it on a very comprehensive, holistic scale, before you make that comparison.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: The Silver Support Scheme is a lifeline for many of our seniors, especially our very senior seniors – maybe those above the age of 80.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I see them every time in Jalan Besar and Whampoa.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: And as Assoc Prof Jamus Lim noted, the Silver Support Scheme is already 10 years old.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: My question for the Minister is whether the Government could consider a more fundamental review of the Silver Support Scheme and in particular, the eligibility criteria; not the levels, but the criteria themselves.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked about the coverage of some of these criteria, like the lifetime CPF contribution.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I think that we should instead review whether the lifetime CPF contribution should even be a criterion for the Silver Support Scheme, keeping in mind that there are a lot more seniors who have lived far beyond their retirement savings.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Those above 80, would not remember what they contributed up to the age of 55, which is the current criteria.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: And the Government now has more sophisticated means testing criteria and mechanisms compared to 10 years ago, when the Silver Support Scheme was first implemented.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Indeed, we constantly review the frameworks, the criteria, as to how we can better support all of our elderly Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Not just all of our elderly Singaporeans, we have also gone upstream to see in their younger working years, through the entire lifespan of their working career, their entire work life journey itself, to see how at different points in time we can provide uplifts to our Singaporeans, fellow citizens.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Having said that, we share the same view, we share the same end objective, as Mr Shawn Loh and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, because we constantly want to look for ways to continue to uplift each and every Singaporean, way into their golden retirement years.
